items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear (ConsistentHashHeader, constructConsistentHash, applyConsistentHash), fields have doc comments and the test names describe intent. Minor gap: type-level doc comments are missing on e.g. `type ConsistentHashHeader struct`.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Follows the plugin pattern: separate consistent_hash.go, IR in constructor.go, apply step in plugin, merge in merge.go (+93 lines), deepcopy/CRD regenerated. Much of the merge code is hidden, so I couldn't confirm the shared dedup/sort helpers or function sizes.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: MinLength=1 on key fields, a CEL rule for disable exclusivity, constructConsistentHash returns an error (TTL parsing), and Validate is registered in the validators list. No swallowed errors visible.

items.name: Multi-policy merge semantics
items.evidence: Merge tests cover the union with higher priority first, canonical order (7 entries ending with sourceIp), sourceIp kept nil when the higher-priority policy leaves it unset, disable precedence, and MergeOrigins.Get("consistentHash") holding both refs. Hidden tests pass.

items.name: Empty spec and disable handling
items.name_zh: 空配置与 disable 处理
items.evidence: XValidation rule "when disable is true, no other fields may be set" on the ConsistentHash type, with the CRD regenerated. Empty {} defaults to sourceIp terminal=false. HigherDisableSuppresses test shows inherited policies are suppressed.
